clue.text: Writer dropping key in ravine or shaft

indicators.note: a key let fall into the ravine word means its letter goes inside it
with dropping, this says the key letter lands inside the ravine word

parts.note: a gorge is a deep ravine
E is a musical key
a well is a shaft sunk into the ground

explanation.surface: An author lets a key fall down a ravine or a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the whole definition; 'dropping' and 'in' together say the key falls inside the ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm wrote under this pen name.

clue.text: Essayist keeps Egyptian chapter lyrical

indicators.note: the essayist holding something means another piece sits inside his pen name

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
EG is an abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: A writer of essays guards a chapter from Egypt in a poetic mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb's Essays of Elia make 'Essayist' a stock crossword pointer to his pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegiac verse is mournful lyric poetry, the mode of the elegy.

clue.text: Animal harness needs a bit of relaxation when crossing river

indicators.note: the relaxation letter goes across and past the river to sit after it

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's harness
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

indicators.note: only a small first piece of relaxation is taken, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A horse in harness wants a moment's rest while fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' gives R from 'relaxation', which comes after DEE once it has crossed the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou of the Arctic are a species of large deer, a kind of four-legged beast.

clue.text: We hear lover betrays nobleman

indicators.note: the words give away a run of letters they contain, revealing the nobleman

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a lover has double-crossed an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' suggests a homophone, but nothing is said aloud: the title is tucked inside 'hear lover'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Learning about German without a diversion

indicators.note: the trimmed learning word goes round the German one
the learning word loses the letter named by the clue's a

parts.note: reading is learning, as in a man of wide reading
the single letter as written
Herr is the German for Mr, so stands for a German man

explanation.surface: Study of German conducted without a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' strips one letter from the learning word, and 'about' then wraps the remainder (REDING) round the German.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that draws attention away from the truth, like a smoked fish laid to throw off hounds.

clue.text: Nest for a year in lake

indicators.note: the year abbreviation sits inside the lake's name

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A bird's home kept for twelve months beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Nine crashed into obstacle that's forgiving

indicators.note: the scrambled number goes inside the obstacle word

parts.note: a let is an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: the letters of nine smash and scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Nine people crash into a barrier, but the owner is tolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' makes NIEN; 'let' meaning hindrance survives in legal English and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful and tolerant, slow to punish.

clue.text: Waits around — is fed a stew of vegetables

indicators.note: the waiting word wraps round the stewed letters

parts.note: lingers means waits about, delays leaving

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about while being served a casserole of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew of' gives ADIESF; 'vegetables' is okra, not fingers of any lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are known in Britain by this name for their long slender shape.

clue.text: Kind offer to pick up Edward

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid
to pick up a signal or remark is to hear it
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Offering to collect a man named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tender-hearted is gentle and compassionate, easily moved to sympathy.

clue.text: I leer at model in studio

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: An artist ogles a sitter in the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, from French.

clue.text: Exploding grenade creates disorder

indicators.note: a bursting grenade scatters its pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb going off causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' is the verb here: to throw into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion, to upset the arrangement of things.

clue.text: One has Irish assembly returning in epic poem

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the assembly's name goes back the other way

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: Someone holds an Irish parliament session in a heroic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail (Dáil Éireann) is Ireland's parliament; 'returning' gives LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is a founding epic of Greek literature.

clue.text: Clergyman always in distress

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the distress word

parts.note: to rend is to tear, and figuratively to distress, as in a heart-rending cry
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A priest is permanently troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and, informally, the name for a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Army volunteers went to announce a dance

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
ran means went, as in the bus ran late
to tell is to announce or make known

explanation.surface: Reservists went off to proclaim a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance in 6/8 time.

clue.text: Desk for display in south-east Mediterranean island

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: the display word goes inside the island name

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
to air views is to display them openly

explanation.surface: A writing table sold for display somewhere in the south-east Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing cabinet with a drop-front surface for writing.

clue.text: Teacher seizes shirt in uproar

indicators.note: the teacher grabbing something means it goes inside his title

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
T stands for the T-shirt, named for its shape

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster grabs a pupil's shirt amid the commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizes' puts T, as in T-shirt, inside SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or excited fuss, as in causing a stir.

clue.text: Perfectionist gives Bob a problem

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S
a tickler is a puzzling or tricky problem

explanation.surface: A fussy person sets a friend called Bob a tough puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a name; it is old British slang for a shilling, written S (from Latin solidus).
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness and correct procedure in every detail.

clue.text: South American in evidence of reincarnation

indicators.note: the word shows the answer plainly within its letters

explanation.surface: A Peruvian native offers proof of past lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled a great empire in the Andes before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Popular humorist supports companion in conversation

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting pieces sit underneath the companion

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
in means fashionable or popular
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A well-loved comedian stands by a friend during a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat or gossip.

clue.text: Type of building predominant in Devon

definitions.note: a phrase standing for somewhere located in that county

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
staple means main or chief, as in a staple product

explanation.surface: A kind of farm structure common across Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the answer is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon on the River Taw.

clue.text: Corruption in Portugal? A German life depends on it!

definitions.note: a phrase describing a nutrient that living things cannot do without

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
rot is decay or corruption
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Is Portugal rotten? A German insists his life hangs on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins build and repair every cell, so all living organisms need them.

clue.text: French working girl set tiger loose

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and run into a new order

explanation.surface: A Parisian shop girl lets a tiger go free.
explanation.definitionFit: A grisette was a young working-class Frenchwoman, often a seamstress, named for her grey dress.

clue.text: Each girl on the train

indicators.note: in a down entry the girl's name sits on top of the rail letters

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
RY is an abbreviation for railway, where trains run

explanation.surface: Every girl is riding on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Every and each both mean all the members of a group, one by one.

clue.text: Singers love rich orchestration

indicators.note: orchestrating arranges parts, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A love song in rich arrangement for vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers.

clue.text: Soldier climbed on to an island

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the soldier's letters go upwards

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner

explanation.surface: A soldier scrambled up onto an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'climbed' reads the gunner's letters upwards, giving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde, and the Aran Islands lie off Galway.

clue.text: Unfair treatment? It's right to get a word in!

indicators.note: the article and abbreviation go inside the right word

parts.note: real can mean right or proper, the genuine article
WD is an abbreviation for word

explanation.surface: Is it fair to let someone have their say?
explanation.walkthrough: A and WD (word) go 'in' REAL; the question mark marks the definition as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is harsh or unjust handling, a bad bargain.

clue.text: Steward takes lithium for comfort

indicators.note: the steward taking the metal means its symbol goes inside him

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval steward or manager of an estate
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A steward takes lithium to feel better.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease pain or distress, to comfort.

clue.text: Tenor appears in mocking novel

indicators.note: the tenor word turns up inside the mocking word

parts.note: guying means making fun of someone
tenor means general character or manner, as in the tenor of a speech

explanation.surface: A singer turns up during the teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenor looks like a singer; it means the gist or manner of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Mannering is an 1815 historical novel by Walter Scott.
